```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

```{r config}
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
source(here::here("R", "compile_functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "plot_helpers.R"))

stock <- cfg$STOCK_SLUG %||% cfg$SPECIES_SLUG
sp <- tolower(cfg$SPECIES_NAME)
area_label <- if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) {
  paste("ICES subareas", paste(unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), collapse = " and "))
} else cfg$REGION
over_cm <- cfg$OVER_CM
fish_label <- paste0("Fishable (≥ ", over_cm, " cm)")
n_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = " ")

dt <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "compiled-data.rds"))
lengths <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "length-data.rds"))
compile_metadata <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "compile-metadata.rds"))
dt$cruiseseries <- order_cruise_series(dt$cruiseseries, dt$year)
cs_cols <- cruise_series_colours(levels(dt$cruiseseries))
lengths <- lengths |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(dt, haul_id, year, cruiseseries, geartype), by = "haul_id")
lw <- compile_metadata$lw
pos <- dplyr::filter(dt, biomass > 0)

# Long format of the two biomass products for figures
products <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::transmute(dt, haul_id, year, month, depth, geartype, cruiseseries,
                   longitudestart, latitudestart, product = "Total",
                   biomass, density = rho_biomass),
  dplyr::transmute(dt, haul_id, year, month, depth, geartype, cruiseseries,
                   longitudestart, latitudestart, product = fish_label,
                   biomass = biomass_fishable, density = rho_biomass_fishable)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(product = factor(product, levels = c("Total", fish_label)))
```

# Purpose

This document describes the compiled IMR bottom-trawl data for the `r sp` (*`r cfg$SPECIES_LATIN`*) survey indices in `r area_label` (stock `r cfg$STOCK_CODE`). It explains and shows the two kinds of data that enter the spatiotemporal sdmTMB models [@Vihtakari2026]: the station-based catches, which give total biomass, and the length measurements, which divide each catch into fishable (≥ `r over_cm` cm) and smaller fish.

The input is the compiled dataset written by the survey-selection document ([`r stock`-2-survey-selection](`r stock`-2-survey-selection.html)), which documents the stock area, haul filter, surveys, gear and timing; those are not repeated here. The output is a judgement of whether the total-biomass and fishable-biomass responses are fit to be modelled, and where their coverage is thin.

# Data

## Data collation

The data flow is shown in @fig-data-flow. Station-level catches give the complete haul roster with true zeros and the total-biomass response. Individual length measurements are used only to divide each positive catch into the fishable and non-fishable parts; they do not change the total.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-data-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Data flow from the IMR Biotic database to the two model responses. Station catches give total biomass directly; individual lengths, converted to weight with the length–weight relationship, give the fishable share of each catch."
flowchart LR
  A["IMR Biotic database<br/>(BioticExplorerServer)"] --> B["Station catches<br/>stnall"]
  A --> C["Individual lengths<br/>indall"]
  B --> D["Haul filter and<br/>survey selection"]
  D --> E["Haul roster with<br/>true zeros"]
  E --> F["Total biomass<br/>per haul"]
  C --> G["Raised length<br/>distribution per haul"]
  G --> H["Weight-at-length<br/>(length–weight fit)"]
  H --> I["Fishable share<br/>of haul biomass"]
  F --> J["Total biomass density"]
  F --> K["Fishable biomass density"]
  I --> K
```

### Station-level data

The station-level dataset has one row per retained bottom-trawl haul. The `r sp` catch weight (`biomass`, kg) is summed over the catch samples of a haul, and hauls without `r sp` in an included survey are true zeros. Swept-area biomass density is

$$
\rho = \frac{B}{d \times w / 1852},
$$

where $B$ is the catch weight (kg), $d$ the towed distance (nmi) and $w = `r cfg$GEAR_WIDTH`$ m the common effective trawl width, giving density in kg nmi^−2^. The density is the model response (`EFFORT: "`r cfg$EFFORT`"` in `config.yaml`); gear type is a fixed effect in the models.

### Individual-level data

The individual-level dataset contains the `r sp` length records from the retained hauls. Lengths are converted from metres to centimetres, and records outside `r compile_metadata$length_limits[1]`–`r compile_metadata$length_limits[2]` cm are removed as gross errors (`r compile_metadata$n_length_outliers` records). When a catch sample contains $m$ measured fish and a catch of $n$ fish, each measured fish represents $n/m$ fish (the raising factor); without a count the factor is one.

## Length-based data

Individual weight is predicted for every measured fish from the length–weight relationship $W = aL^b$ fitted to the survey fish with recorded weight (@fig-length-weight), so that measured and unmeasured weights are treated alike. For fish $i$ in a haul with raising factor $s_i$ and predicted weight $w_i$, the fishable share of the haul biomass is

$$
p = \frac{\sum_{i:\,L_i \ge `r over_cm`} s_i w_i}{\sum_i s_i w_i},
$$

and the fishable biomass is $B_f = pB$, with density $\rho_f = B_f / (d \times w / 1852)$. The fishable part therefore never exceeds the total, and the length data only redistribute the recorded catch. <!-- State how the threshold OVER_CM was chosen (e.g. from commercial length distributions or maturity). -->

Positive hauls without length measurements receive the biomass-weighted mean fishable share of the same survey, or, if no fish were measured in that survey, of the same cruise series and year, or of the cruise series. Zero hauls are zero for both products.

# Analysis

## Dataset overview

The station-level dataset contains `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` hauls from `r min(dt$year)`–`r max(dt$year)`, of which `r n_fmt(nrow(pos))` caught `r sp` and `r n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass_fishable > 0))` caught fishable `r sp`. The individual-level dataset contains `r n_fmt(nrow(lengths))` length records from `r n_fmt(dplyr::n_distinct(lengths$haul_id))` hauls (@tbl-overview). The cruise series differ in the share of positive hauls, in density and in the fishable share of the catch (@tbl-response-by-series).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-overview
tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("Hauls", paste0("Hauls with ", sp), paste0("Hauls with fishable ", sp),
             "Zero fraction, total (%)", "Zero fraction, fishable (%)",
             "Length records", "Hauls with length records",
             "Length records with recorded weight",
             paste0("Positive hauls with fishable share from survey or series mean")),
  Value = c(n_fmt(nrow(dt)), n_fmt(nrow(pos)), n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass_fishable > 0)),
            sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass == 0)),
            sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass_fishable == 0)),
            n_fmt(nrow(lengths)), n_fmt(dplyr::n_distinct(lengths$haul_id)),
            n_fmt(sum(!is.na(lengths$weight_kg))),
            n_fmt(sum(pos$fishable_imputed %in% c("survey mean", "series-year mean", "series mean"))))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Overview of the station-level and individual-level ", sp, " data."))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-response-by-series
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Hauls = dplyr::n(),
    `Positive (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass > 0), 1),
    `Fishable positive (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass_fishable > 0), 1),
    `Median positive density (kg/nmi²)` = round(stats::median(rho_biomass[biomass > 0]), 1),
    `Total catch (kg)` = round(sum(biomass)),
    `Fishable share (%)` = round(100 * sum(biomass_fishable) / sum(biomass), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Station-level responses by cruise series. Density is swept-area biomass density in hauls with ", sp, "; fishable share is the fishable part of the total catch."))
```

## Station-level data

### Spatial distribution

Total and fishable biomass density are mapped for all years combined in @fig-density-map. The fishable fish occur in the same areas as the total catch, but in fewer hauls.

```{r density-map-base}
n_years <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$year)
base_density <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dt, legends = FALSE, base_size = 8,
                                     rotate = TRUE, expand.factor = 1,
                                     land.col = "grey85", land.border.col = "grey60")
density_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_density, ncol = 2, extra = 1, side = 0.4)
```

```{r, fig.height = density_map_height}
#| label: fig-density-map
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Biomass density of total (left) and fishable (right) ", sp, " in all retained hauls, all years combined. Grey crosses: zero catch; circles: positive hauls, size and colour by density (kg per nmi²).")'
base_density +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = dplyr::filter(products, density == 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), shape = 3, size = 0.2, colour = "grey50",
    alpha = 0.4, crs = 4326) +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = dplyr::arrange(dplyr::filter(products, density > 0), density),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart, size = density, colour = density),
    alpha = 0.8, crs = 4326) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "plasma", direction = -1,
                         labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                         name = "Density (kg/nmi²)") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~product) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```

### Through time

The annual mean density and the share of positive hauls show how the raw data change through the time series before any model standardisation (@fig-annual-response). These values mix changes in stock size with changes in survey coverage, gear and season, which the model separates.

```{r}
#| label: fig-annual-response
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual raw data for total and fishable ", sp, ". A: share of hauls with ", sp, ". B: mean biomass density over all hauls (including zeros) with 95 % confidence intervals.")'
annual <- products |>
  dplyr::group_by(product, year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(positive = mean(density > 0), mean = mean(density),
                   se = stats::sd(density) / sqrt(dplyr::n()), .groups = "drop")
prod_cols <- stats::setNames(c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"), levels(products$product))
p_a <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, 100 * positive, colour = product)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prod_cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Positive hauls (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
p_b <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, mean, colour = product)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - 1.96 * se, 0), ymax = mean + 1.96 * se),
                  size = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prod_cols) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean density (kg/nmi²)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v", rel_heights = c(4, 5))
```

### Depth

Depth enters the models as a smooth term. The hauls with `r sp` cover a narrower depth range than the sampling effort (@fig-depth A), and density in the positive hauls varies with depth (@fig-depth B). The depth range of the data limits the depth range of the prediction grid.

```{r}
#| label: fig-depth
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Depth distribution of the data. A: bottom depth of all hauls and of hauls with ", sp, " (densities scaled to the same maximum; the deepest 0.5 % of hauls are outside the plotted range). B: biomass density against depth in positive hauls; lines are descriptive loess smooths, not the model.")'
depth_lim <- c(0, stats::quantile(dt$depth, 0.995, na.rm = TRUE))
depth_hauls <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(dt, group = "All hauls"),
  dplyr::mutate(pos, group = paste("Hauls with", sp))
)
p_a <- ggplot(depth_hauls, aes(depth, after_stat(scaled), fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey50", "#E69F00")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = depth_lim) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Scaled density", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
p_b <- products |>
  dplyr::filter(density > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(depth, density, colour = product)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = depth_lim) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prod_cols) +
  labs(x = "Bottom depth (m)", y = "Density (kg/nmi²)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v", rel_heights = c(4, 5))
```

### Season and gear

Month enters the models as a smooth term and gear type as a fixed effect. Both are confounded with cruise series, because each series is fished in a fixed season with one main gear (see the survey-selection document). @fig-month-gear shows the raw positive densities by month and by gear type within cruise series; differences between gears within the same cruise series are the information the gear effect is estimated from.

```{r}
#| label: fig-month-gear
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Biomass density of total ", sp, " in positive hauls by month (A) and by gear type within cruise series (B), logarithmic scale. Numbers under the month labels and below the boxes are positive hauls.")'
month_n <- dplyr::count(pos, month)
month_lab <- stats::setNames(paste0(1:12, "\n(", month_n$n[match(1:12, month_n$month)], ")"), 1:12)
month_lab <- sub("\\(NA\\)", "(0)", month_lab)
p_a <- ggplot(pos, aes(factor(month, levels = 1:12), rho_biomass)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.4, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, labels = month_lab) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "Month (positive hauls)", y = "Density (kg/nmi²)")
gear_n <- dplyr::count(pos, cruiseseries, geartype)
y_low <- min(pos$rho_biomass) / 3
p_b <- ggplot(pos, aes(cruiseseries, rho_biomass, fill = geartype)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, linewidth = 0.3,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.75, preserve = "single")) +
  geom_text(data = gear_n, aes(cruiseseries, y_low, label = n, group = geartype),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75, preserve = "single"), size = 2.5,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gear_colours()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density (kg/nmi²)", fill = "Gear type") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v")
```

## Length-based data

### Length–weight relationship

The length–weight relationship was fitted on the log scale to `r n_fmt(lw$n)` survey fish with recorded weight, after removing `r compile_metadata$n_lw_outliers` outliers (|standardised residual| > 4). The fit gave $W = `r signif(lw$a, 3)` L^{`r round(lw$b, 3)`}$ with $W$ in kg and $L$ in cm (@fig-length-weight).

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-weight
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Length and weight of ", sp, " with recorded weight in the retained hauls. The line is the fitted length–weight relationship used to predict weight at length.")'
lw_data <- dplyr::filter(lengths, !is.na(weight_kg), weight_kg > 0)
ggplot(lw_data, aes(length_cm, weight_kg)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_function(fun = function(x) lw$a * x^lw$b, colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = over_cm, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Weight (kg)")
```

### Length distributions

The raised length distributions show which part of the population each cruise series catches relative to the fishable threshold (@fig-length-dist). The share of the catch above the threshold differs between cruise series, which is one reason why the fishable and total indices can diverge.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-dist
#| fig-height: !expr 'ceiling(dplyr::n_distinct(lengths$cruiseseries) / 3) * 1.8 + 0.6'
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Raised length distributions of ", sp, " by cruise series (5-cm bins; each measured fish weighted by its raising factor). Dashed line: fishable threshold (", over_cm, " cm). n: measured fish.")'
len_n <- dplyr::count(lengths, cruiseseries, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = paste0("n = ", vapply(n, n_fmt, character(1))))
ggplot(lengths, aes(length_cm, weight = raising, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = over_cm, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = len_n, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~cruiseseries, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Raised number of fish")
```

The length composition also changes through time (@fig-length-year). Because the cruise-series mix changes between years, part of this change reflects survey coverage rather than the stock.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-year
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual raised length composition of ", sp, ", all cruise series combined. Line: median length; ribbon: 10th–90th percentile. Dashed line: fishable threshold. Years with fewer than 10 measured fish are not shown.")'
wq <- function(x, w, p) {
  o <- order(x); x <- x[o]; w <- w[o]
  cw <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  x[which(cw >= p)[1]]
}
lengths |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 10) |>
  dplyr::summarise(q10 = wq(length_cm, raising, 0.1), q50 = wq(length_cm, raising, 0.5),
                   q90 = wq(length_cm, raising, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(year, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = over_cm, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Length (cm)")
```

### Fishable share and length coverage

`r n_fmt(sum(pos$fishable_imputed == "measured"))` of the `r n_fmt(nrow(pos))` positive hauls had measured lengths; the fishable share of the others was taken from the survey or cruise-series mean (@fig-length-coverage A). The annual fishable share of the total catch is shown in @fig-length-coverage B.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-coverage
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("A: positive ", sp, " hauls by the source of their fishable share, by cruise series. B: fishable share of the total ", sp, " catch by year (all hauls combined); point size shows the number of positive hauls.")'
src_cols <- c(measured = "#0072B2", `survey mean` = "#56B4E9",
              `series-year mean` = "#E69F00", `series mean` = "#D55E00", none = "grey50")
p_a <- pos |>
  dplyr::count(cruiseseries, fishable_imputed) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fishable_imputed = factor(fishable_imputed, levels = names(src_cols))) |>
  ggplot(aes(cruiseseries, n, fill = fishable_imputed)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = src_cols, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Positive hauls", fill = "Fishable share from") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
p_b <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(share = sum(biomass_fishable) / sum(biomass), n = sum(biomass > 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, 100 * share)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = "#D55E00") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, name = "Positive hauls") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Fishable share of catch (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_a, p_b, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", align = "v", axis = "lr")
```

### Consistency checks

The checks in @tbl-length-checks confirm that the length allocation is internally consistent.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-length-checks
tibble::tibble(
  Check = c("Fishable biomass exceeds total biomass (hauls)",
            "Largest difference total − fishable below zero (kg)",
            "Positive hauls without a fishable share",
            "Density equals catch / swept area (largest absolute difference)",
            "Length records with raising factor ≠ 1"),
  Value = c(sum(dt$biomass_fishable > dt$biomass + 1e-9),
            format(min(0, min(dt$biomass - dt$biomass_fishable)), digits = 3),
            sum(pos$fishable_imputed == "none"),
            format(max(abs(dt$rho_biomass - dt$biomass / dt$swept_area)), digits = 3),
            n_fmt(sum(lengths$raising != 1)))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Consistency checks of the station and length data.")
```

# Results and recommendations

**Ready for modelling.** The total-biomass response is complete for all `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` hauls, with `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass == 0))` % true zeros. The fishable-biomass response is defined for every haul as well; `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass_fishable == 0))` % of the hauls have no fishable `r sp`.

**Usable with a stated limitation.** For `r n_fmt(sum(pos$fishable_imputed != "measured"))` positive hauls the fishable share is a survey or cruise-series mean rather than a measurement (@fig-length-coverage). The fishable share also depends on the predicted weight at length, so the fishable biomass is a modelled division of an observed catch.

**To examine in the model fits.** Depth, month and gear type all relate to density in the raw data (@fig-depth, @fig-month-gear), but these relations are confounded with cruise series and area. Whether the cruise series needs its own term, and how the changing survey mix affects the indices, is examined in the model fits and validation.
